I've been working this land for 40 years. I know Quzhou's soil and its weather — the dry springs, the heavy summer rains that never quite come when you want them, the cold that sets in by November. My 5 mu is not big, but it is mine, and I know every corner of it.

My land splits naturally into two blocks. About 2.5 mu I've run on the cabbage-longbean-spinach rotation for years. It works — the longbeans put something back in the soil, the spinach clears the field before cabbage comes back. The other 2 mu goes to summer maize, which my household depends on for food and a bit of cash. I keep half a mu for chili on a sunny edge plot near the well head.

For maize I always buy hybrid seed — my neighbor stopped doing this once, ten years ago, and his yield was terrible. Never again. For cabbage I buy improved seed from the county seed shop. For the rest — chili, longbeans, spinach — I use seed I saved myself. I've kept my chili line for fifteen years and it does well here.

I apply compound fertilizer at planting and topdress with urea. The extension station says I use too much nitrogen, but my father did the same and I've never had a bad harvest from over-fertilizing. I'd rather be safe. My well is reliable — I run it when the leaves start to curl or when I know a critical stage is coming. Cabbage caterpillars are my biggest headache; I spray four times on that crop without question.

For tillage I use the small rotary tiller I bought eight years ago. It saves my back. Only on the spinach plot after longbeans do I sometimes just direct-seed without another till pass — the soil is loose enough after the beans.
